ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 45:55 ratio of high-intensity (white) to low-intensity (black) pixels; high-intensity pixels dominate the distal lobes while low-intensity pixels are concentrated in the medial and peduncle regions.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white blobs cover roughly 70% of the left lobe and 50% of the right lobe; black pigmentation extends in a broad V-shape from the notch toward the leading edges, with high-contrast feathered boundaries at the intersection of pigment zones.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep U-shaped depression with a calculated interior angle of approximately 70-80 degrees; depth is roughly 15% of the total lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Irregular serration pattern along the continuous boundary; medial sections show low-amplitude peaks (2-5 pixels), while distal sections transition into high-amplitude, irregular protrusions obscured by parasitic clusters.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex trailing edge curve with a sharp sigmoidal upward sweep at the distal extremities.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense clusters of circular, high-contrast white pixel groupings (barnacles) localized primarily at the fluke tips and intermittently along the leading edge margins.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several dark, unaligned linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) are visible on the high-intensity white field of the left lobe, primarily oriented vertically.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization at the distal tips creates a jagged, non-biological silhouette; small circular depigmented scars are present on the dark medial surface near the peduncle.
other_distinctive_markers: Distinct 'feathering' effect at the transition between black and white pigment zones; prominent cluster of parasites at the extreme right tip creating a trailing fringe.
